summary:
Round five verdict: READY_AFTER_FIXES — four record/provenance fixes in two untracked documents, no code, test or doc-of-record defect.

I re-verified the delta independently rather than arbitrating on the lenses' word. The option-A implementation is correct and minimal. `function_equations` (Tools/semantic_digest.ML:363-381) issues `maps query (0 upto length (binder_types T))` with `Var` placeholders and then `filter keyed_on_const`. The comment's load-bearing claim — that the net matches a query only against keys of the same argument count — is confirmed directly by the probe `scratchpad/fun_optB/net.out`: `bare Const cfk -> 0`, `cfk ?a1 -> 1`, `cfk ?a1 ?a2 -> 0`; `cfpq` only at depth 2; `plainf` only at depth 0. So the counts are disjoint, no entry is returned twice, and `scratchpad/fun_perfA/perf.txt` corroborates it at heap scale (entries returned per pass: current=41, A=41, i.e. option A returns the same set through 8862 instead of 2877 queries, 0.3 ms). The arity bound is sound: a `context fixes` export prefixes the fixed variables, so the exported type's `binder_types` length always covers the key's argument count. `scratchpad/fun_impl/ctx_probe.out` shows the intended end state for the distribution shape (`key = step ?k`, bare query 0 entries, depth-1 query 1 entry, `own_defining_axioms` now 3 props = 1 Defs + 2 simps, no duplication), and `registry_recheck.out` is unchanged at 32 GAINS / 6 class parameters `[]` / `fold2_bit_int.F` unchanged.

S13i discriminates and is placed right. `mentions (own "sens_cfun") "Groups.plus_class.plus"` can only be satisfied through the simps: the Defs axiom is `sens_cfun ?k ≡ sens_cfun_sumC ?k`, and `exists_Const` never sees the type. Measured red-then-green: `scratchpad/fun_optB/sens_R.log:48` is `FAIL S13i` with S13a–h and S14 PASS, `sens_A.log:48` is PASS. Diffing the verified module `scratchpad/fun_optB/semantic_digest_A.ML` against the shipped `Tools/semantic_digest.ML` shows only the `prop_ord` move, the expanded block comment and the inlining of `val arity` — behaviourally identical, so the green measurement transfers to the shipped bytes. The nine wording fixes are each present and true: S13g's `_def_raw` note, `prop_ord` after `class_param_of`, ACCEPTANCE.md's narquil bullet (five same-key enrolments, 23 − 18 = 5, the two new-key facts excluded) and `galmuth_dom` out of the walled list, limitation #8's measured-absence wording plus its closing parenthesis excluding the `context fixes` shape, §7.3 item 1's two facts (nameless `Spec_Rules` item at function.ML:217, no item for an unterminated `function`), the 四条→三条 renumbering, §3.2's constant row, §14's rows, the gate plan's status paragraph.

What survives is one class of defect only: PLAN.md and ACCEPTANCE.md, both about to be committed as the authority and the evidence, under-record this round's own work. Three gaps in PLAN.md (the fourth review round and `review/impl_judge.json` are named nowhere, so "Implementation review F1" at :83 and :392 dangles — and collides with the F1 of the §3 user-decision table at :157; the status block's red-then-green evidence clause omits S13i; §6's subject register, which §9 item 1 quantifies over, was not extended with the `context fixes` subject, so the acceptance criterion silently excludes the only assertion that tests the new code path) and one in ACCEPTANCE.md (it attributes the paid run to "the implemented `Tools/semantic_digest.ML`", which after the commit reads as the module in the tree — and the dates cannot disambiguate, since the run, the title and the §8 F1 stamp are all 2026-09-13). All four are one-clause hand edits in untracked documents; none touches F1-F7 or §8, none touches code, tests or the three docs of record. Nothing blocks 提交 once they are made.

rulings.id: P1 (wording/F5-1 limb four + evidence/R5-1 half one)
rulings.title: PLAN.md never records that a fourth review round happened: `review/impl_judge.json` is named from no line of the plan, so "Implementation review F1" at :83 and :392 dangles — and the token F1 is already bound to a different thing at :157
rulings.reasoning: Verified: `grep -n impl_judge PLAN.md` returns nothing, while `ls ai-artifacts/fun_digest/review/` shows impl_judge.json (24,962 bytes, 17:43) beside the three files the status block names, and HANDOFF item 5 puts `review/*` in the commit set, so the referent will be sitting next to the plan. Both rebutters conceded this limb and I agree with their reasoning on the rest: the parenthesis says "after three adversarial review rounds" and lists exactly those three rounds' records, every clause of which is still true — so appending a fourth file to a list introduced by "three" is the wrong repair, and the count must not simply be raised to four either, since rounds one to three reviewed the PLAN and round four reviewed the CODE. What makes this a defect rather than a nitpick is not list completeness but a dangling cross-reference the round-five delta itself created: the delta added :83 ("measured 2026-09-13, implementation review F1") and :392 ("Implementation review F1 (2026-09-13, evening)") to a document that is declared the authority (HANDOFF:112) and that binds F1 at :157 to the user decision "Direction A". A reader of PLAN.md alone meets a label with no antecedent in the document and a colliding binding for it. That also disposes of wording/F5-5 as a separate item: the collision is real but is cured by giving the second register an antecedent, not by re-labelling an archived ruling id. One clause, by hand (no scripted edits to plan documents).
rulings.fix: In PLAN.md line 6, after "round three found no design defect)" and before " and", insert: "; the CODE was then reviewed in the same directory (`impl_judge.json`, READY_AFTER_FIXES) — the F1 it raised is not the F1 of §3 and is decided in §8". Leave "after three adversarial review rounds" and its three-file list exactly as they are: those three rounds reviewed this plan, and the sentence is true as written. Do NOT bump the rev label — HANDOFF:112 ("Read `ai-artifacts/fun_digest/PLAN.md` rev 2.3 first — it is the authority") is a historical record of the compaction entry point and must not be rewritten to chase it. If this round's ruling is itself archived as a file in `review/`, name it in the same inserted clause.

rulings.title: The status block's red-then-green evidence clause covers S13a–e/S14 only; S13i, the sole assertion that exercises the option-A code, has no red-first record anywhere in the repository
rulings.reasoning: Verified end to end. The clause reads "`Test_Sensitivity` red on the old module for S13a–e/S14 and green after". `grep -rn S13i` over the repository returns only PLAN.md:396 (the bare words "test S13i" inside §8's decision record), Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy:329, and SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_HANDOFF.md:100, which says "implemented with test S13i and the nine wording fixes; all tests green again" — green only, never red-first. The measurement exists but only in session scratch: `scratchpad/fun_optB/sens_R.log:48` is `FAIL S13i` and `sens_A.log:48` is `PASS`. HANDOFF item 5 says "Never commit probe files or logs", so after 提交 the repository would carry a red-then-green record for every discriminating assertion except the one guarding the newest code path. The evidence rebutter conceded this half outright and I confirm its one substantive correction: the two reds are against DIFFERENT baselines and must not be folded into one clause. I checked `scratchpad/fun_impl/Test_Sensitivity_Red.thy` (16:54) directly — `grep -c 'S13i\|sens_cfun'` returns 0, it carries S13a–h and S14 only — so S13a–e/S14 were red on the pre-change module, while S13i was red on the post-round-four, pre-option-A module, which is exactly why sens_R.log shows S13a–h PASS with only S13i failing. Writing S13i into the existing list would assert a measurement nobody took.
rulings.fix: In PLAN.md, extend the clause at :10-11 so the two baselines stay separate. Replace "`Test_Sensitivity` red on the old module for S13a–e/S14 and green after" with "`Test_Sensitivity` red on the old module for S13a–e/S14 and green after, S13i red on the pre-option-A module and green after". Change nothing else in the block; "no open items" and the `Test_All`/registry-re-check clauses stay as they are.

rulings.title: §6's subject register was not extended with the `context fixes` subject, and §9 item 1 keys the acceptance criterion to §6 — so the stated criterion does not range over S13i
rulings.reasoning: Verified. `grep -n 'context fixes' PLAN.md` gives 81, 186, 392 and nothing in §6; `grep -n S13i PLAN.md` gives 396 only. §6 is demonstrably maintained as a register, not a sketch — its bullets match Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy subject for subject (`sens_fun`, the MERGE pin repeated on `sens_pfun`, `sens_pfun` with the `accp` assertion, the three controls, the explicit negative "No `instantiation` subject") — and the delta added a fourth positive subject and a tenth assertion to the file while leaving §6 at the old shape. §9 item 1 states the criterion as "every new assertion §6 annotates as discriminating FAILS on the current code and PASSES after", so by its own quantifier S13i is outside it, and the plan states no criterion that deleting the `sens_cfun` subject would violate beyond §8's prose. I accept the evidence rebutter's two corrections and they do not save the item: the re-run scenario as the challenger wrote it is wrong (a future re-run checks the whole file green; the red-first clause is inherently one-shot), and §8:392-396 does give the subject a weak guard. What remains is a real desync in a document committed as the authority, and it is the same gap as P2 seen from the other end. The wording lens rejected its own version of this (F5-3) partly on the premise that §6 was edited by the delta — §6 WAS edited, but only its `CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN` documentation bullet for ruling D2, not its subject list, so the rejection does not carry. Elegance decides the shape of the fix: because §9 item 1 quantifies over §6 instead of listing assertions itself, one §6 bullet restores the invariant "§9's red-first set = §6's discriminating annotations" and §9 needs no edit at all.
rulings.fix:
By hand, one bullet inserted in §6 at PLAN.md:316, after the `function sens_pfun` bullet (:313-315) and before the "Controls" bullet, so the positive subjects stay together:

"  - `context fixes sens_k … fun sens_cfun`: under a `context fixes` block the
     fixed variable becomes a parameter on export and the registry key is the
     application `sens_cfun ?sens_k` (§2), which the bare-constant query misses
     and the per-argument-count lookup of §4 finds.  Assert the props mention
     `Groups.plus_class.plus` (discriminates: neither the exported type
     `nat ⇒ nat ⇒ nat` nor the body-free `Defs` axiom can supply it).  FAILS on
     the pre-option-A module, PASSES after."

Do not touch §9 item 1 — it quantifies over §6, so the new bullet brings S13i inside the criterion by itself. Do not touch Test/Test_Sensitivity.thy: the subject (:276-281), the assertion (:329-330) and its comment (:328) are already right. Do NOT adjust the "§14 table two rows" count in §6's documentation bullet at :321 — round four settled that count as loose with no consequence (D7, reject).

rulings.title: ACCEPTANCE.md attributes the paid run to "the implemented `Tools/semantic_digest.ML`", which after the commit reads as the module in the tree — and that module gained the option-A query path three and a half hours after the run
rulings.reasoning: I rule against the rebutter here, on one fact its defence rests on and which does not hold. The rebutter argues the record is self-dating and that an auditor who follows its own opening citation lands on the right chronology. But the dates cannot disambiguate: the run is 17:05 (/var/tmp/qiyuan/fun_accept_logs/host_run2.log 17:06:37), ACCEPTANCE.md's title is stamped "(2026-09-13)", and PLAN.md §8's F1 bullet is stamped "2026-09-13, evening" — the same day throughout, so nothing in the record separates the two module versions. In the committed tree the phrase "the implemented `Tools/semantic_digest.ML`" denotes the file sitting beside it, which carries the per-argument-count registry query the run never executed; the record is the sole end-to-end evidence for this change and is exactly what a later auditor would cite. That is a concrete misattribution risk, not a style remark, and the round-four judge ruled the same document's attribution class `fix` twice. I reject the challenger's proposed wording as firmly as the rebutter does: it would put a forward-looking claim about a later code version into a git-tracked record, supported only by `sweep_old.txt` vs `sweep_A.txt` in a /tmp scratchpad that is never committed, and would create a standing obligation to re-verify that clause on every future amendment of the module. The correct repair is the rebutter's own fallback — date the module, assert nothing about the later one, and state only what PLAN.md §8/§9 already say.
rulings.fix: In ACCEPTANCE.md:3, replace "PLAN.md §9 item 3, run with the implemented `Tools/semantic_digest.ML`." with "PLAN.md §9 item 3, run at 17:05 with `Tools/semantic_digest.ML` as implemented at the time; the F1/option-A amendment recorded in PLAN.md §8 came out of the implementation review that follows (§9 item 4) and is not exercised here." Add nothing about what option A does or does not move — that claim belongs to the registry re-check and `Ctx_Probe`, which are already attributed correctly in SCOPE "Round five" and HANDOFF item 5. Leave the rest of ACCEPTANCE.md untouched.

rulings.title: PLAN §8's "the §14 row is rewritten (both cells) as §5 says" no longer describes what shipped
rulings.reasoning: The finding's concrete failure is factually wrong, and I checked the cells myself. §5 at :280-283 prescribes cell 1 = "参数改名使 digest 变化（归一化已撤销，2026-09-13）" and cell 2 = "digest 在 hash 前被做了变换" — the separator falls after the closing parenthesis, so §5's cell 2 holds only a failure mode and sits correctly under the header 缺了会怎样 (:725, "| 断言 | 缺了会怎样 |"). Restoring §5's literal cells therefore cannot "put the behaviour F6′ wants back into the failure column"; it would at worst yield a second acceptable wording of the same row. What is left is a letter-versus-substance gap in which the substance is on §8's side: §8:397-400 is recording which of §5's two options the user took, and "(both cells)" is the marker distinguishing a full rewrite from a partial edit of the old row. Both cells were rewritten and both of §5's sentences are present in the shipped row at CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN.md:743; the only deviation is that the date-stamped note sits in cell 2 and the literal ML assertion in cell 1 — which §14's 断言 header demands and which §5 (b) itself calls "the standing guard". That deviation is not an unreviewed accident: round four's ruling D4 states the tension in so many words, weighs it against F7 ("Tests, comments and the plan's details are the implementer's call", PLAN.md:163), blesses the placement, and prescribes the shipped row character for character. The delta applied that ruling verbatim. Asking now for an amendment the ruling deliberately did not require, on the strength of a consequence that does not follow, is a letter-level nitpick.

nitpicks_named: code/R5-2 — "PLAN.md's status line still enumerates the red-on-old-module set as S13a–e/S14, omitting S13i", raised as standalone bookkeeping: correctly rejected by its own filter as a re-raise of round four's R4-5 reject. (Note the substance is NOT what my P2 rules on: P2 requires the two baselines to be stated separately, because S13i was never run against the old module — the fix this item asked for would record a measurement nobody took.)

code/R5-3 and wording/F5-4 and evidence/R5-2 — "PLAN §7 and limitation #8 still explain the surviving locale gap with 'the bare-constant query returns 0'": correctly rejected, three times over. I verified the sentence is literally true of the shipped code — Tools/semantic_digest.ML:376 is `maps query (0 upto length (binder_types T))`, whose n = 0 case IS the bare-constant query, and it still returns 0 for those constants — and that the decisive clause precedes it in both places (doc/invalidation_limitations.md:308-310, "theory 可见的登记表里没有任何键提到该 locale 常量…（CENSUS (b)：wildcard 枚举 19 条，无一相关）"), which forecloses every argument count at once. Limitation #8's closing parenthesis already tells the reader the query shape changed. A rewording request for a true, non-load-bearing clause.

code/R5-4 — "the function_equations block comment presents the registry key's two shapes as if exhaustive": correctly and harshly rejected. It is "consider adding two words to a comment", which the scope names as a nitpick; the challenger conceded "None demonstrable" and every factual claim in the comment as true, and its one speculative failure (a maintainer deleting `keyed_on_const`) is refuted by that filter's own one-line justification sitting immediately below it.

wording/F5-5 — "'F1' now names two different things inside PLAN.md": correctly rejected as a standalone finding (both sites qualify the identifier as "implementation review F1"; nothing was coined, so the consistent-terminology rule is not engaged; a document-wide re-labelling of an archived ruling id is scope this delta cannot contain). Its underlying discomfort is cured as a side effect of my P1 clause, which gives the second register an antecedent.

wording/F5-6 — "the two foreign uncommitted edits the round-four judge ordered kept out of the commit are still in the working tree": correctly rejected; not a wording finding and not a finding of this round. Tools/entity_position.ML and archive/tests/test_migrate_from_collection.py showing as modified in `git status --short` is the expected state — they are foreign edits that are supposed to stay in the tree and out of this commit, exactly as impl_judge.json's summary and SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_HANDOFF.md:104-106 already record.

evidence/R5-4 — "the post-fix Test_Sensitivity / Test_All green runs left no artefact on the shipped bytes": correctly rejected. It is round four's R4-5 re-raised for the post-fix runs, and a round-four reject is out of bounds this round; it also asks for a measurement that cannot change the delta. I independently closed the gap it worried about by diffing scratchpad/fun_optB/semantic_digest_A.ML against the shipped Tools/semantic_digest.ML: the only differences are the `prop_ord` move, the expanded block comment and the inlining of `val arity`, so the measured green transfers to the committed bytes.

evidence/R5-5 — "§2 and §9 item 1 still price 'the registry query' as one query per constant": correctly rejected with the finding's own concession of no concrete failure. scratchpad/fun_perfA/perf.txt puts the extra queries at 2877 → 8862 per whole-heap pass for 0.3 ms total, inside the 3–5 µs figure's own precision; the imagined harm is a threefold over-estimate of a nine-millisecond number with no downstream consequence.

wording/F5-3 — "the F1 amendment updated PLAN §2/§4/§8 but not §6 or §9 item 1": rejected by its filter, but the rejection does not hold and I uphold the substance as ruling P3. The filter's stated ground was that "§6 WAS edited in this delta" — §6 was edited only in its CHECK_OUTDATE_PLAN documentation bullet (ruling D2's two facts), not in its subject register, which is the half that matters, since §9 item 1 quantifies over exactly that register. The evidence lens's R5-3 made the same point with the mechanism attached, and its rebutter conceded it.

wording/F5-2 — kept by its filter, rejected by me above: its concrete failure misreads where §5's cell separator falls, and the placement it objects to is round-four ruling D4's prescribed wording, blessed under F7.
